request: Analyze GSE128078 for the paper (Whole blood human transcriptome and virome analysis of ME/CFS patients experiencing post-exertional malaise following cardiopulmonary exercise testing): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.
decision_maker: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) Claude Code subagent session

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq of whole blood (PAXgene, Nugen Ovation rRNA/globin depletion), HiSeq 2500 PE100 (S2.5.p1)
final.subjects: 14 female ME/CFS cases and 11 age/sex-matched sedentary controls (S2.2.p1, ABS.p1)
final.sample_inclusion: two samples of one subject (day 3 and day 7) with <40% transcriptome coverage removed (S3.3.p1, S1 Fig A)
final.primary_estimand: Within-subject change in whole-blood gene expression after cardiopulmonary exercise testing (day 2, 3, 7 versus pre-exercise day 1), separately in ME/CFS patients and in controls (Table 3 lower block); secondary: ME/CFS-vs-control difference per day and difference in pre-to-post change (S3.3.p2).

low-VO2 and test-retest ME/CFS subsets vs regular repeat exercise (Table 3) - subset labels not deposited

paper_threshold.stated_text: fold change > +-1.5, p-value < 0.05, and adjusted p-value (FDR) < 0.1%

final.paper_method: Partek Flow 5.0: STAR + Cufflinks FPKM on hg38 RefSeq; per-gene multimodel (normal/lognormal/lognormal-shrinkage/NB/Poisson) chosen by AICc (S2.5.1.p1)
final.paper_results: No exercise DEGs in either group at any day (Table 3); 19 unique disease/subset DEGs, mostly low-coverage false positives (S3.3.p2, TAB4)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: The exercise question is answered in Table 3 lower block (Day 1 vs Day 2/3/7 within CFS and HC) and S3.3.p2 (pre vs post in CFS compared with controls). Day 1 and day 2 blood is drawn within 2 h before each CPET (S2.5.p1), so day 1 is the unexercised baseline and days 2, 3, 7 are about 24 h, 48 h and 6 days after the first test. The FDR text says '<0.1%' but every listed DEG in Table 4 has FDR 0.02-0.10, so the operative cutoff was FDR 0.1; treated as the paper threshold, with the literal 0.001 kept as audit.

checks: GEO contact Chiu Lab UCSF matches the paper's sequencing site (S2.5.p1)
99 whole-blood samples, 14 ME/CFS + 11 controls x 4 days (55 + 44; G12 day 7 absent) match ABS.p1 / S2.5.p1
treatment field 'Cardiopulmonary exercise' and timepoints 1/2/3/7 match S2.5.p1

matrix.reasoning: Deposited file is named isoforms_FPKM; GEO data_processing states FPKM from cufflinks 2; values are non-integer (39% integer only because of zeros), median about 0, max 4.96e5. Transcripts (NM_/NR_ RefSeq) were mapped to symbols with MyGene.info (40184/43497 mapped, 23293 genes) and summed per gene, as Cufflinks computes gene FPKM. No counts deposited, so count models are not possible.

final.formula: ~ 0 + day + subject (fitted separately within CFS and within HC)
final.secondary: change-from-day-1 difference CFS vs HC (paired change); CFS vs HC per day (associational); other day pairs exploratory

design.reasoning: Table 3 lower block tests Day 1 vs Day 2/3/7 separately within CFS and HC, so disease is a stratum and day the factor with subject blocking (S2.5.p1: each subject gives 4 samples). Disease-group comparisons are cross-sectional (associational), run as secondary. The 'all days combined' CFS vs HC comparison needs a random subject effect that the runner cannot fit; not run. Low-VO2 / test-retest subsets cannot be built: per-subject classification is not deposited.

deviations: limma on log2(FPKM+1) instead of Partek multimodel
gene FPKM summed from deposited hg19 Cufflinks isoform FPKM instead of the paper's hg38 STAR/Partek gene FPKM
log2FC from limma on log scale instead of Partek linear fold change

method.reasoning: Policy: linear FPKM goes to log2(x+1) then limma. Subject blocking as fixed effect within strata.

final.deviation_note: Paper: |FC| > 1.5, p < 0.05, FDR < '0.1%'. Table 4 lists DEGs with FDR up to 0.10, so FDR < 0.1 is applied; the literal FDR < 0.001 is the audit rule. The extra p < 0.05 cannot be encoded alongside padj in one rule; with BH, padj < 0.1 and p >= 0.05 requires more than half of genes to be significant, so it is not binding here.

threshold.reasoning: S2.5.1.p1 and TAB4. FC 1.5 converted exactly to log2(1.5) = 0.5849625.

caveats: Different upstream processing (hg19 Tophat2/Cufflinks isoforms deposited vs hg38 STAR/Partek gene-level in paper)
Low-VO2 and test-retest subset comparisons not reproducible: subject classification not in GEO
All-days CFS vs HC (paper 6 DEGs) not run: needs a random subject effect
